title: First band: the pupils' yard band
summary: The first band was a group of Perkins's pupils who played in his yard on Sundays. Clark lists the members.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: After you learned to play then what was your first job? Do you remember your first band you played in?

Well the first band I ever played in, the boys that were taking lessons there, we set up a little brass band just amongst us scholars. And he'd take us one Sunday evening in the yard. He'd sit us in his yard. And that's how we started playing. Every other Sunday we would go and we'd sit in that yard. They had about ten of us.
Some did and some didn't. Some did and some didn't. Who were they?
Do you remember any of them?

Well Anderson Minor, we called him Gulley, he was taking bass at that time. And Joe Harris, which is dead, he was taking trombone. And another fella by the name of Jefferson Butler, he was a trumpet player, he's dead. And fella by the name of Henry Williams, he don't play anymore now. He's a minister now. And Felix Goff, clarinet. What did Henry Williams play?
And Felix Goff, he was on the clarinet and had another boy on the E flat clarinet called Stewart. I don't know what happened to him. He went out of the picture all at once, I don't know.

No, his name was Stewart. He had another name now, I just can't, but that was his first name, Stewart. Little short fella. And our drummers was a boy by the name of Jumerville, and another boy by the name of Dito, which Dito is dead now. Jumerville was the bass drummer and Dito was the snare drummer. And we just kept on with that little band like that so funny. We just worked ourselves up in two bands.
No, we didn't name him. You didn't work professionally?
